subject: german
topicName: Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: German has four cases that show the role of a noun in a sentence. Each case affects the articles (der/die/das), adjectives and pronouns.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Two-way prepositions: movement towards = ACCUSATIVE (Wohin?); location/position = DATIVE (Wo?). "Ich gehe in die Stadt" (acc — movement) vs "Ich bin in der Stadt" (dat — location).

steps.title: German Exam Tips — Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive
steps.body: 1. For Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Cases: Nominative, Accusative, Dative and Genitive, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Fill in the correct article: Ich gebe ___ Mann ___ Buch. Ich fahre ___ Berlin. | Q: Which case after these prepositions: mit, für, in (location), in (movement)?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch (dem = dative masculine after geben to someone; das = accusative neuter direct object). Ich fahre nach Berlin (nach takes dative, but with place names nach + no article for  | mit → dative. für → accusative. in (location/Wo?) → dative. in (movement/Wohin?) → accusative.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use a range of tenses (present, past, future) to access higher marks Include opinions with reasons (ich finde... weil... / meiner Meinung nach...) Check case endings (nominative, accusative, dative) before finishing Get word order right: verb-second in main clauses, verb-at-end after dass/weil/wenn Use complex structures: subordinate clauses, modal verbs, separable verbs Include cultural references to German-speaking countries (DACH)
